title: Audit the edge firewall's 11 rules and propose a clean rule set
situation: Auditors flagged the main edge firewall. It has 11 rules built up over the years, including a 'temporary' allow-everything rule that was meant to be removed on a Friday, remote desktop open from the internet for a vendor, and guest Wi-Fi allowed to reach everything. There is also no final rule that blocks anything not allowed.
your_task: Read the rules top to bottom and find duplicates and rules hidden by earlier rules.
Flag traffic that crosses network zones it should never cross, such as internet to internal or guest to database.
Flag insecure protocols, overly broad rules, missing logging and rules with no owner or ticket.
Compare the current rule set with the remediated one and confirm the fixed version has no findings.
why_it_matters: One allow-everything rule cancels out the whole firewall. Remote desktop open to the internet is one of the most common ways ransomware gets in.
done_when: The current rule set scores 0/100 (grade F), with all 15 findings explained and a fix for each.
The remediated rule set scores 100/100 (grade A) and ends with an explicit, logged deny-all rule.
The Tor-blocking rule is moved above the website allow rule so it actually works.
Vendor remote access goes through the multi-factor authentication jump hosts instead of straight from the internet.

glossary.Firewall rule: An instruction that allows or blocks certain network traffic.
glossary.First match wins: The firewall checks rules in order and uses the first one that fits.
glossary.Shadowed rule: A rule that never takes effect because an earlier rule already matches the same traffic.
glossary.Demilitarized zone (DMZ) / screened subn: A separate network area for public-facing servers, kept apart from internal systems.
glossary.Segmentation: Splitting a network into zones so a problem in one does not spread to the others.
glossary.Default deny: A final rule that blocks anything not allowed by an earlier rule.
glossary.Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP): A way to control a Windows computer remotely over port 3389.

talking_point: Audited an 11-rule edge firewall that scored 0/100, documented 15 findings including an any/any rule and internet-exposed RDP, and delivered a segmented 9-rule replacement that scored 100/100.
